services.name: Interaction_SynchronizeResponseState
services.behavior: Drains ACTOR_RESPONSE_COUNTER, compares the six current display bytes at 0xFF7E29 with the pending bytes at 0xFF7E30, copies the pending value when it has advanced, and sets HUD_DISPLAY_UPDATE_PENDING.

services.name: Hud_RunPendingDisplayPresentation
services.behavior: When HUD_DISPLAY_UPDATE_PENDING is set, clears C000/E000 and non-player actor records, prepares the temporary presentation, runs AnimationVM/render submission and the shared frame service for 0x293 iterations with the 16-phase cadence, then applies a fade and clears the temporary actors.

evidence.trigger: Interaction_SynchronizeResponseState clears FFF0F1 on entry and sets it only after copying an advanced six-byte display value from 0xFF7E30 to 0xFF7E29.
evidence.presentation_window: Hud_RunPendingDisplayPresentation clears the pending flag, sets SCENE_RESOURCE_MODE to 4, renders the initial temporary actor state, services 0x293 iterations, selects the short frame helper while FRAME_PHASE_COUNTER&0x0F is below 6, and finishes with palette fade plus actor cleanup.
evidence.call_path: The pending-display service is called from the level/scene reset path after the response-state synchronization and before active-scene initialization.

limitations: The static path establishes a pending display presentation but does not assign a user-facing name such as score, bonus, or reward without runtime/UI correlation.
The two one-instruction RTS entries at 0x001B0134 and 0x001B0136 remain intentionally unnamed aliases/helpers.
conclusion: The display-update flag and its long presentation consumer are now named as a distinct HUD synchronization path, separate from the actor response counter drain and from scene-resource dispatch.
